=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Scope:** This review is based on the Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), the full draft SPA, or the Seller's Schedule 7. Figures are as the Seller describes them and should be checked against source documents.

## Overall view

The package shifts almost all known risk to the Buyer. It combines a low-value general cap, a deductible-style basket, a short claims window, a data-room-wide disclosure, an anti-sandbagging clause, and deferred or unquantified treatment of known liabilities. Several items the Seller's own disclosure identifies as open are either left to post-Completion or characterised as immaterial without evidence.

The Seller's "market context" and "FINAL, not to be re-opened" language does not bind us. Those are assertions by the other side. If principals did settle these terms, we should ask for the written record of that agreement and test each position on its merits.

## Key departures and reasoning

**1. General cap (cl 12.1): AUD 4.8m (20%)**
A 20% cap is at the top of the Seller's own quoted range and well below what a Buyer should expect where known exposures already total several million dollars. Known items alone (Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k, supplier renewals AUD 330k) come to roughly AUD 4.1m before any Bluefen revenue loss (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue). Known exposures should be dealt with by specific indemnities or price adjustments, not left to a general cap that is already consumed.

**2. Basket and de minimis (cl 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k excess-only**
- The basket is roughly 1% of price, and is structured as a deductible. Only the excess is recoverable, so the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every claim.
- Push for a **tipping basket**: once the threshold is crossed, the whole claim is recoverable.
- Lower the de minimis, or remove it for related claims. Related claims should be aggregated.
- Carve fundamental/title and tax warranties out of both thresholds entirely.

**3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, applied to all Claims by default**
- 18 months is short for a SaaS business with revenue-contract, privacy and tax exposure that may take time to surface.
- The Seller's proposed default (limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise) should be reversed. Longer periods should apply by default to fundamental, title and tax claims.
- Propose 24–36 months for general warranties, and at least the statutory limitation period (confirm the NSW position under the Limitation Act 1969, including whether contractual shortening is effective) for fundamental and title warranties.
- Tax claims should run at least through the ATO amendment period plus a buffer.

**4. Fundamental and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits**
This is a clear departure. Title to shares and capacity should be capped at the purchase price (or 100% of price) with the longest limitation period. Administrative simplicity is not a reason to weaken them.

**5. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance, and limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)**
- These provisions must expressly exclude fraud, and fraud should not be capped or time-limited.
- Exclusive remedy should not bar specific indemnities, equitable relief, or claims for fraud and misrepresentation in the Disclosure Letter.
- Non-reliance should not stop the Buyer relying on express warranties in the SPA.

**6. Data-room-wide general disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7)**
This is the most serious departure. Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, plus the statutory registers and public records, effectively discloses against all warranties. A Buyer would be left with no warranty claim for anything it could find in the data room, which is the entire diligence record.
- Reject general disclosure. Disclosure should be specific, fair-disclosure standard, against identified warranties only.
- Disclosure should not cure breaches of fundamental or tax warranties.

**7. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3)**
The Buyer should not lose claims because it knew of a matter or could have discovered it from the data room. This clause combined with item 6 would leave the Buyer without recourse for the known issues. Push for a **pro-sandbagging** clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice any claim. Known issues should be covered by specific indemnities, which do not depend on warranty breach.

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; Disclosure 2)**
- The Seller's wording treats the consent as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent", which is not the same as a final, unconditional consent in agreed form.
- The conditions in clause 11.3 of the Bluefen contract are not addressed.
- Reasonable endeavours is weak. Push for all reasonable endeavours with the Seller bearing costs.
- Make receipt of a final written consent, with the 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by the Buyer, a condition precedent. Include a walk-away right and a price adjustment or specific indemnity for lost revenue if consent is not obtained or is conditional.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; Disclosure 3)**
- A release "to be provided following Completion" is unacceptable on a debt-free, cash-free basis. Repayment and discharge of all security should occur at Completion from the price, with a PPSR discharge and release deed delivered as a completion deliverable.
- Confirm the funds flow pays out the full amount, including break costs, and that the PPSR search is clean.

**10. Employee bonuses (cl unspecified; Disclosure 5; funds flow)**
- AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are not in the funds flow. Under a debt-free, cash-free structure, transaction-related employee liabilities should reduce the price or be paid by the Seller.
- The disclosure does not address payroll tax (NSW), superannuation guarantee or on-costs. These should be included in the leakage/price adjustment, with a specific indemnity for any unpaid amounts.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; Disclosure 4)**
- The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, which does not cover the Buyer's real exposure. That exposure includes IP ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and any unpaid fees.
- The AUD 180k open fee is unverified. Require evidence of payment or a settlement before Completion, or retain the amount from the price.
- Require a confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 IP as a condition precedent, plus a specific IP chain-of-title indemnity.

**12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; Disclosure 6)**
- Describing this as "not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a finding. The disclosure itself says the investigation is preliminary, scope and access are unknown, and notification may be required.
- The affected data (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) for about 1,240 people may engage the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), including the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme. The Company will inherit any obligations and liability.
- Requirements: a completed forensic assessment before signing, a specific indemnity covering notification, regulatory, complaint, remediation and third-party claims (with no cap or basket), a retention or escrow sized to the risk, Buyer input into the investigation, and a privacy compliance warranty.
- Obtain privacy specialist input on notification timing and obligations.

**13. Office lease (Disclosure 7)**
Confirm whether landlord consent is required for a change of control or share sale. If yes, make it a condition precedent. If notification alone is required, make it a Completion deliverable.

**14. Mossvale assignment restriction (Disclosure 9)**
Confirm in writing that no consent is required for the share sale. If there is any doubt, obtain a consent or a waiver as a condition or specific indemnity.

**15. Supplier renewals (AUD 330k; Disclosure 8)**
The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs without evidence. The disclosure does not confirm whether they are unavoidable, terminable, or accrued. Require a full contract schedule, treat committed amounts as a price adjustment or leakage item, and restrict new commitments between signing and Completion without Buyer consent.

**16. Tax and IP warranties ("settled under the general regime")**
This is inadequate. Require full tax and IP warranties, a pre-Completion tax indemnity (not subject to cap or basket), and a longer survival period. Tax due diligence should be completed before signing.

**17. Title (Disclosure 10; DD-012)**
The share register identifies the Seller as holder of 100% of the shares, but it is the Seller's source document. Before signing, obtain:
- An ASIC company extract
- A certified copy of the share register
- Confirmation of no options, convertibles, or encumbrances (including a PPSR search)
- A title warranty and fundamental indemnity

**18. Information currency**
Disclosures and data room are stated as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down of diligence and disclosures, with no new disclosure permitted to cure a breach without Buyer consent.

## Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1: Must-have before signing**
1. Replace the data-room-wide general disclosure with specific disclosure only (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7).
2. Add a pro-sandbagging clause and remove the anti-sandbagging clause (cl 8.3).
3. Carve fraud out of all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
4. Raise the fundamental and title cap to the purchase price, with longer time limits, and remove them from the general basket and caps (12.1–13).
5. Specific indemnities, uncapped and outside the basket, for: Ironquay IP, the export/privacy incident, Bluefen consent failure, Riverlark (if not repaid at Completion), bonuses, supplier commitments, and pre-Completion tax.
6. Bluefen final written consent (with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied) as a condition precedent, with walk-away rights.
7. Riverlark repayment and PPSR discharge at Completion, not after.
8. Reconcile the funds flow to include bonuses and transaction-related employee costs as price deductions.

**Priority 2: Commercial negotiation**
9. Tipping basket, lower de minimis, and related claims aggregation (12.2).
10. General warranty cap raised (we should target a materially higher figure, to be set by the deal team against the known exposures), with a longer general time limit of 24–36 months (12.1, 12.3, 13).
11. Reverse the default limitation rule so longer periods apply to fundamental, title and tax claims.
12. Escrow or retention sized to the known and unquantified exposures.
13. Interim covenants restricting new supplier and contract commitments without Buyer consent.

**Priority 3: Verification and confirmations**
14. Independent title verification (ASIC extract, certified register, PPSR search).
15. Confirm landlord and Mossvale consents in writing.
16. Forensic report on the export incident before signing; privacy specialist advice on notification.
17. Full tax due diligence and tax warranties.
18. Bring-down diligence and disclosure as at signing and Completion.
19. Request the written record of the principal-level agreement the Seller refers to, and verify each "settled" position against it.

## Caveats

- This review relies on the Seller's summaries. The underlying DD documents and full SPA draft need to be checked.
- Specific NSW limitation periods, contractual shortening rules, payroll tax and superannuation treatment, and Privacy Act obligations should be confirmed with NSW counsel, tax advisers and privacy specialists before positions are finalised.
